summary: Defines a way to write GeoJSON as a sequence of separate items, with the media type application/geo+json-seq. It builds on JSON text sequences so very large geographic datasets can be read piece by piece instead of all at once.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 8142 defines a sequence format for GeoJSON so a large dataset can be read one object at a time. Each GeoJSON text is marked with a record separator and ends with a line feed.

subtitle: A stream format for reading large GeoJSON datasets one object at a time.

tldr.problem: Very large geographic datasets can be difficult to process as one JSON document, especially when they contain many features and coordinates.
tldr.mechanism: Each UTF-8 GeoJSON text is preceded by an ASCII record separator and followed by a line feed, allowing incremental parsing.
tldr.outcome: The format permits sequences of different GeoJSON object types and registers the media type application/geo+json-seq.

today: The unit metadata lists RFC 8142's status as Proposed Standard. The RFC defines the GeoJSON text sequence format and its media type.

sections.title: Why Use a GeoJSON Sequence
sections.content:
Geographic datasets can contain tens of thousands or millions of features, often with large coordinate arrays. A single large JSON document can therefore be difficult to produce or parse as a whole.

RFC 8142 specializes JSON text sequences for GeoJSON. A sequence can contain one or more GeoJSON objects and can be processed incrementally rather than as one FeatureCollection, Feature, or Geometry.
sections.plainLanguage: A large map dataset can be sent as a stream of separate objects. A reader can process each object without waiting for the whole dataset.

sections.title: Separating the GeoJSON Texts
sections.content:
Each item is a GeoJSON text encoded in UTF-8. An ASCII record separator character comes before it, and a line feed follows it.

Each JSON text must contain one GeoJSON object. A sequence may mix Geometry, Feature, and FeatureCollection objects, and the format allows both pretty-printed and compact GeoJSON texts.
sections.plainLanguage: A record-separator character marks the start of each GeoJSON object, and a line feed marks its end. The sequence can contain different kinds of GeoJSON objects.

sections.title: Interoperability Considerations
sections.content:
The record separator lets producers and parsers use any valid GeoJSON form without requiring a canonical layout. However, compact GeoJSON with no internal newlines may work with more existing parsers that expect newline-delimited compact JSON.

The RFC also notes that sequences that do not assign extra meaning to the order of objects are more interoperable in distributed systems where order and exactly-once delivery are difficult to guarantee.
sections.plainLanguage: The format does not require one exact spacing style for GeoJSON. Compact objects without internal newlines may be easier for existing line-based tools to handle.
